phd.title: Research on Agricultural Products Volume Estimation Method Based on Depth Imaging and Machine Learning Technology
phd.shortTitle: Agricultural Products Volume Estimation via Depth Imaging & ML (Ph.D. Dissertation 2023)
affiliations: College of Engineering, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing, China
phd.venue: Nanjing Agricultural University · Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Engineering: Agricultural Electrification and Automation Engineering (Supervisor: Prof. Chen Kunjie)
phd.status: Ph.D. Monograph · Sept 2017 - Dec 2023 · 500+ Chapter Citations
phd.teaserCaption: Doctoral end-to-end depth imaging, 3-D point-cloud surface reconstruction, morphological feature extraction, multi-family machine learning regression, processing-latency testing, and statistical validation pipeline developed at Nanjing Agricultural University (2017-2023).
phd.tldr: Doctoral dissertation (Nanjing Agricultural University, 2017-2023, Supervisor: Prof. Chen Kunjie) establishing calibrated RGB-D imaging, occlusion-splitting geometry, 3-D point-cloud reconstruction, and machine learning regressors for non-contact volume and mass grading across tomatoes, eggs, and poultry carcasses.
phd.abstract: Accurate, non-contact size and weight grading in horticultural packing houses and poultry processing lines remains constrained by irregular three-dimensional commodity geometry, mutual fruit or egg occlusion on moving conveyors, and ambient illumination shifts. Conducted from September 2017 to December 2023 in the College of Engineering at Nanjing Agricultural University under Prof. Chen Kunjie, this doctoral dissertation formulates and validates depth-imaging and machine learning pipelines for agricultural product volume and mass estimation across five linked empirical investigations. Calibrated Kinect RGB-D sensors acquire multi-orientation depth frames that are filtered, background-subtracted, and transformed into 2-D contour descriptors, active shape cut masks, and 3-D reconstructed surface-integration meshes. Single-commodity regression models benchmarked across tomatoes, intact eggs, and dressed poultry establish RBF Support Vector Regression (RBF-SVR), Exponential Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Bayesian-regularized artificial neural networks, and Bagged Decision Trees as reliable inline estimators: RBF-SVR achieves 97.06% mass accuracy and 96.94% volume accuracy on cherry tomatoes (allometric power law M = 1.312 V^0.9551, R² = 0.9824); Exponential GPR attains R² = 0.984 (RMSE = 1.175 cm³) on isolated eggs and 1.080 to 1.294 cm³ under partial occlusion via M-circle contour fitting; concave-convex polygon splitting resolves touching tomato clusters at R² = 0.982 for volume and R² = 0.971 for mass; Active Shape Models partition broiler carcasses into commercial cuts (whole carcass R² = 0.9981); and 25-model 3-D surface reconstruction benchmarks confirm Bagged Trees achieve R² = 0.9988 (RMSE = 5.335 cm³, ARE = 2.125%) in under 1.6 s per carcass with paired t-test agreement (P < 0.05).

phd.resultsSummary: Across five experimental studies and 25 evaluated regression families spanning Support Vector Regression, Gaussian Process Regression, Decision Tree ensembles, Kernel Approximation, and Artificial Neural Networks, combining calibrated depth morphology with 3-D surface reconstruction consistently yields R² ≥ 0.982 on held-out postharvest samples. Paired two-sample t-tests between Bagged Tree predictions (1,420.874 ± 191.456 cm³) and physical Water Displacement Method reference measurements (1,412.736 ± 182.634 cm³) confirm agreement (P < 0.05) at < 1.6 s end-to-end processing time per moving carcass.
contributions: Formulated calibrated RGB-D acquisition geometry (0.7 m overhead horticultural belt and 1.2 m × 2.0 m side-view poultry shackle rig) eliminating manual caliper or water-displacement contact.
Developed occlusion-tolerant contour segmentation combining concave-convex polygon approximation for clustered tomatoes and contour curvature plus k-closest M-circle centers for grouped eggs.
Constructed Active Shape Models and 3-D point-cloud surface integration pipelines extracting anatomical cut boundaries, major/minor axes, convex area, eccentricity, and volumetric descriptors.
Evaluated 25 regression architectures across training, validation, and held-out test partitions, verifying statistical equivalence against physical WDM measurements in under 1.6 s per item.

detailSections.title: Chapter Study I: Single Cherry Tomato Volume & Mass Calibration (J. Food Eng. 2019)
paragraphs: Multi-orientation Kinect depth acquisitions established how sensor height calibration (0.7 m above the 0.5 m conveyor belt) records surface height alongside 2-D silhouette descriptors. Across five candidate regression models, RBF-SVM reached 97.06% accuracy in mass estimation from 2-D features and 96.94% in volume estimation using combined 2-D and depth descriptors.

An empirical power-law calibration M = 1.312 V^0.9551 translated vision-estimated volumes directly into fruit mass on held-out test samples at R² = 0.9824 and RMSE = 15.84 g, creating an inline proxy for produce density sorting.

detailSections.title: Chapter Study II: Splitting Occluded Tomato Clusters on Moving Belts (Int. J. Food Prop. 2021)
paragraphs: Packing-line belts rarely isolate single fruits cleanly; mutual contact distorts projected silhouettes and breaks naive area-to-volume regressors. Concave and convex contour vertex detection combined with polygon approximation separates touching multi-tomato clusters cleanly prior to feature computation.

Evaluated across seven regression algorithms trained on isolated tomato geometry, RBF-SVM reached R² = 0.982 (RMSE = 1.2683 cm³) for fruit volume and Bayesian-regularized neural networks achieved R² = 0.971 (RMSE = 1.468 g) for fruit weight across isolated and clustered runs.

detailSections.title: Chapter Study III: Infrared-Depth Chicken Egg Volume & M-Circle Segmentation (J. Food Eng. 2020)
paragraphs: Hatchery and table-egg grading lines present ellipsoidal geometry compounded by tight tray packing and specular shell reflections. Contour curvature analysis paired with a k-closest M-circle-center fitting algorithm separated both simple adjacent pairs and complex multi-egg clusters.

Across 13 trained regression models using non-contact infrared depth descriptors, Exponential Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) achieved R² = 0.984 and RMSE = 1.175 cm³ on isolated eggs, sustaining 1.080 cm³ under simple occlusion and 1.294 cm³ under complex occlusion.

table.title: Exponential GPR Accuracy Across Egg Occlusion Regimes (13 Models Evaluated)

detailSections.title: Chapter Study IV: Broiler Carcass & Anatomical Cut Weight Estimation (Poultry Sci. 2021)
paragraphs: Whole-carcass inspection masks uneven value across commercial poultry cuts. This chapter formulated an Active Shape Model (ASM) capable of segmenting overhead broiler depth frames into drumsticks, breasts, wings, and head-neck regions under processing-plant ambient illumination.

Among five evaluated regression families, Bayesian-regularized neural networks predicted whole-carcass (R² = 0.9981) and head-neck mass (R² = 0.9847), whereas RBF-SVR excelled across articulated cuts (wings R² = 0.9896, breast R² = 0.9352, drumsticks R² = 0.9129).

table.title: Active Shape Model Cut Segmentation & Per-Part Weight Accuracy

detailSections.title: Chapter Study V: Live Conveyor 3-D Carcass Reconstruction & 25-Model Benchmark (Poultry Sci. 2024)
paragraphs: The culminating experimental study replaced static 2-D projections with real-time 3-D surface reconstruction on moving shackle conveyors imaged from a calibrated 1.2 m height and 2.0 m standoff with Kinect v2. Background subtraction, ROI cropping, boundary smoothing, and point-cloud alignment yield watertight triangular meshes whose geometric surface-integration volume joins nine 2-D and 3-D morphological predictors.

Benchmarking 25 regression architectures across Regression Trees, SVRs, GPRs, Kernel Approximation, Tree Ensembles, and Neural Networks identified Bagged Trees as top performer (test R² = 0.9988, RMSE = 5.335 cm³, MAE = 4.950 cm³, MSE = 28.462 cm⁶, ARE = 2.125%), finishing end-to-end acquisition, reconstruction, and inference in under 1.6 s across 30 timed carcasses.

detailSections.title: Literature Taxonomy, Calibration Physics & Continuity at SAAIL Lab (Zanzibar)
paragraphs: Alongside five experimental systems papers, the doctoral synthesis mapped vision-based metrology across live birds, carcasses, cuts, and eggs (Poultry Science 2021 Review, 144 citations; 503 combined citations across all six doctoral publications), isolating low-quality mesh granularity (5-10% sensitivity) and background illumination shifts as dominant deployment failure modes.

At SAAIL Lab (IIT Madras Zanzibar), those exact calibration and occlusion lessons inform current lightweight computer vision pipelines for Zanzibar export clove grading, smallholder foliar disease diagnostics under domain shift (DGS-Bench, CropGuardNet), and point-of-care edge vision systems.

msc.title: Intelligent Control and Monitoring System Based on Arduino for the Greenhouse Environment
affiliations: College of Engineering, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing, China
msc.venue: Nanjing Agricultural University · Master of Science (M.Sc.) in Engineering: Computer Science and Technology (Supervisors: Prof. Bai Zhentian & Prof. Xu Huanliang)
msc.tldr: Embedded microcontroller and multi-sensor greenhouse automation architecture for real-time microclimate monitoring and actuation.
msc.abstract: Controlled-environment greenhouse horticulture demands responsive telemetry and actuation without prohibitive industrial controller costs. Developed as an M.Sc. thesis at Nanjing Agricultural University (2016), this work designs and validates a low-cost Arduino-based intelligent greenhouse monitoring and closed-loop control platform integrating temperature, relative humidity, soil moisture, and ambient illumination sensors with relay-driven ventilation, irrigation, shading, and supplemental lighting actuators for automated protected crop management.
contributions: Engineered a low-cost Arduino embedded greenhouse controller integrating continuous air temperature, relative humidity, volumetric soil moisture, and lux sensing.
Implemented hysteresis-bounded relay actuation driving irrigation pumps, ventilation fans, and shade motors.
Established the embedded hardware sensing baseline extended into modern edge AI and agricultural IoT telemetry at SAAIL Lab.
